name: Teams, invitations and who can do what
matches: remove a member from the team
remove a member from the workspace

failureModes.prompt: Should the database itself refuse to show one organisation's data to another, even when the app code has a mistake?
failureModes.why: a query written without the organisation check shows one company's private data to another, and a database rule blocks that

options.label: Enforced in the database as well
options.consequence: more setup, and one missed check in the code cannot expose another company

options.label: Checked in the app code only
options.consequence: simpler, and one missed check shows a company's data to strangers

failureModes.recommended: Enforced in the database as well
failureModes.provenBy: a test that signs in as a member of one organisation and asserts every list and lookup returns nothing from another organisation, with the app check removed

failureModes.prompt: When someone is removed from a team, should they lose access immediately, including on devices where they are signed in?
failureModes.why: removal often follows someone leaving the company, which is when continued access causes the most harm

options.label: Immediately, on every device
options.consequence: needs a membership check on each request, and a removed person sees nothing more

options.label: When their session expires
options.consequence: simpler, and a removed person keeps access for hours or days

failureModes.provenBy: a test that removes a member while they are signed in on another device and asserts their next request is refused

failureModes.prompt: Should every change to someone's role be recorded with who made it and when?
failureModes.why: without a history nobody can tell who gave a person admin rights, and the history cannot be rebuilt later

options.label: Record every role change
options.consequence: a small history table, and disputes about access can be settled

options.label: Keep only the current role
options.consequence: simpler, and nobody can tell who granted admin rights

failureModes.provenBy: a test that changes a member's role and asserts a record of the old role, the new role, who changed it and when

failureModes.prompt: Should an invitation work only once, and only for the email address it was sent to?
failureModes.why: a forwarded or posted invitation link can otherwise let a stranger join the team and see its data

options.label: Once, for the invited address only
options.consequence: a forwarded link is useless to anyone else

options.label: Anyone with the link can join
options.consequence: easier to share, and a posted link lets people outside the team join

failureModes.recommended: Once, for the invited address only
failureModes.provenBy: a test that accepts an invitation, asserts a second use is refused, and asserts a different signed-in address cannot accept it

failureModes.prompt: If the owner of a team leaves, how should someone else take over?
failureModes.why: a team whose only owner has left is unable to change billing, roles or settings without our help

options.label: The owner hands over before leaving
options.consequence: a short feature to build, and teams are never left without an owner

options.label: Our support staff reassign it
options.consequence: nothing to build, and every handover needs one of our staff

options.label: Require a second owner
options.consequence: no team is ever without an owner, and small teams must name two

failureModes.recommended: The owner hands over before leaving
failureModes.provenBy: a test that hands a team to another member and asserts the new owner can change billing and roles while the old owner cannot

failureModes.prompt: If the price depends on team size, should the bill change automatically when members join or leave?
failureModes.why: a bill that does not match the team size either overcharges customers or gives away seats for free

options.label: Change the bill automatically
options.consequence: needs a link to billing, and charges always match the team

options.label: Adjust bills by hand
options.consequence: nothing to build, and bills differ from the real team size until someone fixes them

options.label: Price does not depend on team size
options.consequence: nothing to keep matched, and large teams pay the same as small ones

failureModes.provenBy: a test that adds and removes a member and asserts the billed seat count matches the member count after each change
